title: Strings & structured parsing
outcome: Turn text exports into meaningful, validated records.

steps.title: 1. Preserve information
steps.text: Decide which whitespace or case is meaningful. strip removes surrounding whitespace, not internal spacing. split with maxsplit preserves a remainder.
steps.code:
line="name:  radio: bench A  "
key,value=line.split(":",1)
print(key.strip(),value.strip())

steps.title: 2. Use the format parser
steps.text: CSV can contain quoted commas. JSON can contain booleans and null. Use csv and json instead of splitting or eval.

steps.title: 3. Validate complete strings
steps.text: A prefix match does not validate a whole identifier. re.fullmatch checks the entire pattern. Use re.escape for literal text embedded in a pattern.

steps.title: 4. Bytes are not characters
steps.text: Choose an encoding explicitly. A byte count measures encoded data, not the number of visible characters. Decode only where the input contract identifies the encoding.

steps.title: 5. Keep parsing separate
steps.text: A parser produces structured observations. A validator decides whether they meet requirements. Do not turn a parse failure into an empty healthy inventory.
